solutions.check: grid rebuilt from the blog's light list (unique); every answer written into it with each crossing agreeing

clue.text: Inn in Granada, so popular in retrospect

indicators.note: in retrospect says the hidden letters are read backwards
the clue word that says the letters sit inside the next words

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: A tavern in the Spanish city of Granada that was once a favourite, looking back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'in retrospect' turns ADASOP, the run inside 'Granada, so popular', backwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A posada is the Spanish word for a roadside inn or hostelry, used in English too.

clue.text: Tennis player once putting some butter on bread

parts.note: a pat is a small flat portion of butter
bread is slang for money, cash

explanation.surface: A former tennis star spreading a bit of butter on a slice of bread.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'putting ... on' sets PAT above CASH. 'Bread' is the money slang, not the loaf.
explanation.definitionFit: Pat Cash, the Australian, won the Wimbledon men's singles in 1987 and has long since retired.

clue.text: Hospital close to square in smart Notts town

indicators.note: in says those pieces go inside the word for smart

parts.note: swell is an old word for fashionable or smart

indicators.note: close to says the hospital letter sits right beside the square word, following it

parts.note: square means unfashionable, out of date: out
H is the map and road-sign abbreviation for hospital

explanation.surface: Looking for a hospital near the square in an elegant Nottinghamshire town.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Square' is the old slang for unfashionable, the opposite of 'in'; 'close to' means right beside, and 'in' is the container signal. Notts is the usual short form of Nottinghamshire.
explanation.definitionFit: Southwell is a small minster town in Nottinghamshire (Notts), an English county.

clue.text: Unrealistic criminal ready to pinch millions

indicators.note: to pinch means to grab and hold, so one piece is gripped inside the other
criminal suggests the word ready has been treated badly and its letters scrambled

parts.note: M is the standard abbreviation for million(s)

explanation.surface: A crook all set to steal millions has a fanciful plan.
explanation.walkthrough: 'criminal' rearranges READY into DREAY, and 'to pinch' puts M inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone dreamy has their head in the clouds, out of touch with practical reality.

clue.text: Follows article on modern technology in edition of Times

indicators.note: in says those letters sit inside the reworked newspaper title
an edition is a version produced afresh, so the word Times is reworked into a new order
on in an across clue puts the article after the technology letters

parts.note: IT is information technology
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Someone tracks a news item about modern tech in an issue of The Times.
explanation.walkthrough: 'edition of' signals a fresh arrangement of the newspaper's name, giving IMTES; 'on' in an across clue means placed after, and 'in' is the container signal.
explanation.definitionFit: To imitate someone is to copy or follow their example.

clue.text: Holding head in arms, Mike worked out source of trouble

indicators.note: holding says the rearranged letters wrap round another piece
worked out suggests the letters of arms and Mike are reshaped into something new

parts.note: a chief is a head, a leader

explanation.surface: Mike, head in his arms, finally figured out what was causing the trouble.
explanation.walkthrough: 'worked out' shuffles the two words into MISMAKER, and 'Holding' makes that the outer piece. 'Head' looks like part of the despairing pose but is the leader.
explanation.definitionFit: A troublemaker who stirs up strife is the cause of the bother.

clue.text: In French, you will get zero in test — will this help?

parts.note: tu is the familiar French word for you

indicators.note: in puts the zero inside the word for test

parts.note: a trial is a test
O looks like the figure zero

explanation.surface: A French learner asks whether this will help them avoid scoring nothing in the exam.
explanation.walkthrough: The definition is a question: a session of tuition is what helps a struggling student.
explanation.definitionFit: A tutorial is a small teaching session meant to help a student with their studies.

clue.text: Olympic cyclist's brisk speed mentioned by commentator

indicators.note: a commentator speaks the word, so we go by how it is said, not spelt

parts.note: a trot is a brisk pace, between a walk and a run

explanation.surface: A broadcaster remarks on how fast an Olympic cyclist is riding.
explanation.definitionFit: Laura Trott (now Kenny) won several Olympic gold medals for Britain in track cycling.

clue.text: WWI poet joining army division shortly

parts.note: the SAS (Special Air Service) is a unit of the British Army
shortly means soon

explanation.surface: A First World War poet is about to enlist in an army unit.
explanation.definitionFit: Siegfried Sassoon wrote celebrated poems about the trenches of the First World War.

clue.text: Word of appreciation initially unusual in Athenian's letter

parts.note: ta is British informal for thank you

indicators.note: initially picks the opening letter of the word unusual

explanation.surface: A thank-you that turns up, unusually, in a letter from someone in Athens.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Letter' means a letter of the alphabet, not correspondence.
explanation.definitionFit: Tau is the nineteenth letter of the Greek alphabet, so one an Athenian would use.

clue.text: Shows jobs no longer available?

parts.note: ex means former, no longer current
positions are jobs, posts

explanation.surface: Exhibitions are put on featuring vacancies that have already been filled.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as a whole, 'jobs no longer available' gives former posts.
explanation.definitionFit: Expositions are large public exhibitions or displays, i.e. shows.

clue.text: Goes off with crew aboard a boat

indicators.note: aboard says the pieces are carried inside the word for a

parts.note: per means a or each, as in five pounds a head
eggs that go off are said to addle, so goes off gives addles
a team is a crew

explanation.surface: Someone leaves with the crew on board a vessel.
explanation.walkthrough: The little word 'a' does real work: it means 'each', as in 'per head'. 'aboard' is the container signal. Eggs that go off are said to be addled.
explanation.definitionFit: A paddle steamer is a steam-driven vessel propelled by paddle wheels.

clue.text: Sorry, imprisoning a maiden in a hut

indicators.note: imprisoning says one piece is locked up inside another

parts.note: a shed is a hut
M is the cricket abbreviation for a maiden over

explanation.surface: Someone regrets keeping a young woman locked up in a hut.
explanation.walkthrough: 'imprisoning' is the container signal; the inner pair lands after the second letter of the hut word. M for maiden comes from cricket scoring.
explanation.definitionFit: Being sorry about what you have done is to feel shame over it.

clue.text: Man's name and address shortly taken by hotel

parts.note: H is hotel in the NATO phonetic alphabet

indicators.note: shortly says the word for address is cut short, its last letter lost

parts.note: an oration is a formal speech, an address

explanation.surface: A man gives his name and address, briefly, to a hotel receptionist.
explanation.walkthrough: 'address' is a speech, not where someone lives; 'taken by' just puts H in front.
explanation.definitionFit: Horatio is a male first name, borne by Nelson and by Hamlet's friend.

clue.text: Closely follow untrustworthy type

definitions.meaning: to follow at someone's ..., as a dog is told to
an old slang term for a cad or rotter

explanation.surface: Tail closely a shady character.
explanation.definitionFit: A dog brought to heel follows closely; a heel is also a scoundrel.

clue.text: To Nigella, a false claim

indicators.note: false suggests the letters are not genuine as they stand and must be rearranged

explanation.surface: An untrue assertion is made to Nigella, the TV cook.
explanation.walkthrough: 'false' rearranges TO NIGELLA A. Nigella Lawson is a well-known British television cook.
explanation.definitionFit: An allegation is an assertion, usually of wrongdoing, made without proof yet.

clue.text: One contrary female accepts a drink? Can't be true

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral for one

indicators.note: accepts says the woman's name takes the drink inside it

parts.note: Mary, Mary, quite contrary is the nursery rhyme
gin is a drink

explanation.surface: A perverse woman agrees to a drink; that can't really be so.
explanation.walkthrough: The nursery rhyme 'Mary, Mary, quite contrary' gives MARY. The definition is a phrase meaning 'not real', an adjective in sense.
explanation.definitionFit: Something imaginary exists only in the mind, so it cannot be real or true.

clue.text: Not so well after first parts of this horrifically riveting tale of suspense

indicators.note: after says the word for not so well comes after the opening letters
first parts of picks the opening letter of each of the next three words

parts.note: iller means more ill, not so well

explanation.surface: Feeling worse after the opening of this horribly gripping suspense story.
explanation.definitionFit: A thriller is a novel or film built on suspense and excitement.

clue.text: Like clones, nevertheless

definitions.meaning: clones are identical, every one alike
a phrase meaning even so, in spite of that

explanation.surface: Like copies of one another, nevertheless.
explanation.definitionFit: Clones are indistinguishable copies; the phrase also means 'even so' in speech.

clue.text: Current in stream dispatched hunter

indicators.note: in says the current letter goes inside the rearranged letters
dispatched suggests the letters of stream are sent off and rearranged

parts.note: I is the physics symbol for electric current

explanation.surface: A hunter was swept away by the current in a stream.
explanation.walkthrough: 'dispatched' rearranges STREAM into ARTEMS; 'in' puts I inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Artemis was the Greek goddess of hunting, often shown with a bow.

clue.text: Theatre seats, neither front nor back available? Unbelievable

indicators.note: says the word loses both its first and last letters

parts.note: the stalls are the ground-floor seats in a theatre

explanation.surface: Seats at the theatre, with no front or back rows to be had? Hard to believe.
explanation.walkthrough: 'neither front nor back available' takes both S's off STALLS. A tall story is one hard to credit.
explanation.definitionFit: A tall tale is an exaggerated, implausible story, hence tall meaning hard to credit.

clue.text: Irritating fellow first to leave barge

indicators.note: first to leave says the opening letter of the word departs

parts.note: blighter is British slang for an annoying person

explanation.surface: An annoying man is the first to get off the barge.
explanation.walkthrough: 'barge' is the definition, a noun, not the verb meaning to push.
explanation.definitionFit: A lighter is a flat-bottomed barge used to ferry goods to and from ships.

clue.text: Little woman's a female 5

definitions.note: points to the answer at 5-down, a troublemaker or prankster

parts.note: Jo March is one of the four sisters in Little Women; the 's adds an S
her refers to a female

explanation.surface: A girl from Little Women is described as a female troublemaker.
explanation.walkthrough: '5' means the solution of 5-down. 'Little woman' is Jo March from Louisa May Alcott's novel.
explanation.definitionFit: One who teases and kids people playfully causes mild mischief, a prankster.

clue.text: Premiership champions given cut

definitions.meaning: the winners of the league are the best team, the leading side
a cut of beef taken from the hindquarter

explanation.surface: The football league winners are given the chop.
explanation.walkthrough: The Premiership is the top English football division. Topside is a lean joint of beef from the leg.
explanation.definitionFit: The champions are the leading team; topside is also a butcher's cut of beef.

clue.text: Chubby person, say, keeling over after dessert

indicators.note: after puts the turned letters behind the dessert

parts.note: pud is British informal for pudding, dessert

indicators.note: keeling over in a down clue turns the letters so they read upwards

parts.note: eg, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A plump person, for instance, collapsing after the pudding course.
explanation.walkthrough: 'keeling over' turns EG into GE.
explanation.definitionFit: Pudge is informal for fat or a podgy person.

clue.text: Wise sovereign today is invested

indicators.note: invested has the sense of being clothed, so one word wears the other around it

parts.note: a king is a sovereign ruler
now means today, at present

explanation.surface: A wise monarch is crowned today.
explanation.walkthrough: 'is invested' reads as a coronation but means the word for today is placed inside KING.
explanation.definitionFit: Knowing means shrewd, well informed, showing understanding.

clue.text: Work next weekend?

parts.note: a literary work, and, for a puzzle printed early in March, the end of next week falls in that month's midpoint

explanation.surface: Someone asks if they will have to work next weekend.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Work' is a book, not labour: George Eliot's novel. The rest is a date joke about the puzzle's publication in early March.
explanation.definitionFit: Middlemarch is the 1871 novel by George Eliot, and read as two words it also names a date.

clue.text: Fitting carpets evenly

indicators.note: evenly picks the letters in the even positions of carpets: second, fourth, sixth

explanation.surface: Fitting carpets so they lie flat and even.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt means suitable or appropriate for the occasion.

clue.text: Sheep-farm workers, quiet breeders not registered to start with

parts.note: sh is the call for quiet

indicators.note: not says the following letter is to be left out

parts.note: rearers are those who raise animals, breeders

indicators.note: to start with picks the opening letter of registered

explanation.surface: Quiet farm workers who breed sheep but weren't registered at first.
explanation.walkthrough: 'registered to start with' gives R, and 'not' drops it from REARERS to leave EARERS.
explanation.definitionFit: Shearers clip the fleece off sheep, a key job on any sheep farm.

clue.text: You run after brother on a donkey?

indicators.note: after puts the you and run pieces behind brother and a

parts.note: ye is an old form of you
R is the cricket abbreviation for run

explanation.surface: You chase your brother while riding a donkey.
explanation.walkthrough: The question mark admits a playful definition: an animal that brays is a 'brayer'.
explanation.definitionFit: A donkey brays, so it may jokingly be called one that brays.
